provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and calibration pending.

title: Customer Support: Recover a Missed Delivery Promise
prompt: You are a support representative for fictional Fern Home. A customer says, "My desk was promised yesterday. I stayed home all day, and tracking has not moved. I need it for work tomorrow." The order is paid, and the carrier status says only "in transit." Company policy lets you investigate and request a delivery update. A refund or replacement needs supervisor approval; you cannot promise a date without carrier confirmation. The interviewer is the customer.
blurb: Acknowledge a missed delivery promise and agree accurate, owned next steps with a frustrated customer.

rubric.label: Understand the practical impact
rubric.description: Acknowledges the failed promise and asks what resolution matters.

anchors.0: Dismisses the inconvenience or blames the customer for relying on the estimate.
anchors.2: Apologizes for the missed expectation and asks about the needed outcome.
anchors.4: Clarifies work timing and availability, summarizes the preferred resolution, and avoids making the customer repeat known order details.

rubric.label: Offer accurate options
rubric.description: Uses policy and evidence to propose the next action.

anchors.0: Promises tomorrow delivery or guarantees an unapproved refund.
anchors.2: Opens a carrier investigation and explains approval limits.
anchors.4: Uses the carrier response window to set a concrete investigation plan and requests supervisor review if the customer’s need cannot be met.

rubric.label: Close the communication loop
rubric.description: Owns follow-up without equating response time with delivery time.

anchors.0: Tells the customer to keep refreshing tracking with no owner or next contact.
anchors.2: Agrees a follow-up update and records the issue.
anchors.4: Confirms update timing and an agreed contact channel, distinguishes an update from a delivery guarantee, and records the customer’s preferred outcome for the next owner.

reference.scenario: You are a support representative for fictional Fern Home. A customer says, "My desk was promised yesterday. I stayed home all day, and tracking has not moved. I need it for work tomorrow." The order is paid, and the carrier status says only "in transit." Company policy lets you investigate and request a delivery update. A refund or replacement needs supervisor approval; you cannot promise a date without carrier confirmation. The interviewer is the customer.

facts.value: The customer can accept delivery after 16:00 tomorrow but cannot stay home for another full day. They prefer receiving the desk over a refund if the timing is reliable.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about the customer’s priority or availability

facts.value: The carrier escalation team responds within four business hours. The support system can set a callback and route a supervisor request; no delivery date has been confirmed.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about investigation timing, follow-up, or escalation options

model_points: The customer lost time and needs a usable work arrangement; acknowledge both. Ask whether timing, replacement, or refund is most helpful before choosing a resolution.
The carrier’s four-hour response window supports a promised update, not a promised delivery. Escalate for evidence and seek supervisor approval for options outside the representative’s authority.
Record availability and preferences so the customer does not have to restart the story. A useful closing says who will contact them, when, and what happens if the carrier still cannot confirm a date.

probes.question: Which supplied fact confirms a delivery date?

probes.trigger: candidate offers an apology but no action
probes.question: What will happen after this call, and when will the customer hear from you?

fair_alternatives: A supervisor escalation at the customer’s request is reasonable even while the carrier investigation is pending.
A written update is as acceptable as a callback when the customer agrees to that channel.
red_flags: Dismisses the inconvenience or blames the customer for relying on the estimate.
Promises tomorrow delivery or guarantees an unapproved refund.
Tells the customer to keep refreshing tracking with no owner or next contact.
follow_ups: Write a closing that promises a support update while accurately describing the unconfirmed delivery.
reference.exemplar_answer: I am sorry the promised delivery cost you a day at home. I understand reliable timing matters more than a refund if we can still meet your needs. I will ask the carrier escalation team for a confirmed status and set an update within their four-business-hour response window. That is an update promise, not a delivery guarantee. I will record your after-16:00 availability and request supervisor options if the carrier cannot provide a workable date.

interviewer_notes: Play a disappointed customer without abusive behavior. When asked, explain the time constraint and preferred outcome. Reward accuracy and ownership rather than compensation beyond authority. Use only supplied facts; say when something is unknown. Accept plain language and equivalent approaches. Assess the demonstrated decisions, not accent, confidence, credentials, or access to particular employers. This is a fictional exercise; do not imply real actions were performed.

learning_drills.title: Separate two promises
learning_drills.prompt: Write a closing that promises a support update while accurately describing the unconfirmed delivery. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
